options.why: Treats the diagonal cut as if it were parallel to a side of the rectangle.
Counts four pieces as though both diagonals had been drawn instead of one.
Stops the diagonal before the opposite corner, creating a shape not shown by the cut.

questions.solution_text:
A corner-to-corner diagonal divides the rectangle into two congruent halves.
$2$ right-angled triangles

options.why: Moves the triangle away from the sloping gap, so the outside boundary is not rectangular.
Places the triangle outside the matching-height strip instead of filling the right-hand gap.
Makes no rearrangement, leaving the original parallelogram rather than a rectangle.

questions.solution_text:
The left triangle matches the gap beside the sloping right edge.
Translate it to the right edge.

questions.question_text:
A $42\text{ cm}^{2}$ shape is cut into pieces and all pieces are rearranged without gaps or overlaps.
What is the new area?

options.why: Doubles the area because there are several pieces, even though no copy was added.
Halves the area because the shape was cut, although all pieces are still used.
Adds an arbitrary amount for the changed outline even though rearranging preserves surface.

questions.solution_text:
Every piece is still used once, so no surface is gained or lost.
$42\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text:
All pieces from a $30\text{ cm}^{2}$ shape are rearranged.
Two pieces overlap by $5\text{ cm}^{2}$, and this is the only overlap.
How much area is visibly covered?

options.why: Uses the total piece area but ignores that the 5-square-centimetre overlap is covered twice.
Adds the overlap even though overlapping reduces the visible union of the pieces.
Subtracts the 5-square-centimetre overlap twice instead of once.

questions.solution_text:
Subtract the part counted twice among the pieces.
$30-5=25$
The visible area is $25\text{ cm}^{2}$.

questions.question_text:
A $28\text{ cm}^{2}$ collection of non-overlapping pieces is arranged inside an outline.
The only uncovered region is a $6\text{ cm}^{2}$ gap.
What area does the outline enclose?

options.why: Reports only the pieces and omits the uncovered gap inside the outline.
Subtracts the gap even though it lies inside and adds to the enclosed area.
Adds the 6-square-centimetre gap twice instead of once.

questions.solution_text:
The outline contains both the pieces and the gap.
$28+6=34$
The outline encloses $34\text{ cm}^{2}$.

questions.question_text: Which move can join two congruent triangles to form a parallelogram?

options.text: Rotate one triangle $180^{\circ}$, then translate it
Enlarge one triangle, then translate it
options.why: Changes the size of one piece, so the matching sides no longer make the intended parallelogram.

options.text: Cut both triangles into smaller pieces
options.why: Introduces unnecessary new cuts when the two congruent triangles already have matching sides.

options.text: Place one triangle directly on top of the other
options.why: Creates complete overlap instead of joining the pieces to form a larger boundary.

questions.solution_text:
A half-turn reverses the copy so a corresponding side can meet the first triangle.
Rotate one triangle $180^{\circ}$, then translate it.

questions.question_text:
A seven-piece puzzle makes a square.
A second design uses only six of the pieces with no overlaps.
Which statement is true?

options.text: The second design has smaller area

options.why: Applies area preservation despite one original piece being omitted from the second design.

options.text: The second design has larger area
options.why: Treats a more spread-out outline as greater area even though one piece is missing.
Ignores that removing a positive-area piece must reduce the total area used.

questions.solution_text:
The second design omits one positive-area piece.
The second design has smaller area.

questions.question_text:
Ava and Ben each use every piece from the same dissection once, with no gaps or overlaps.
Ava makes a rectangle and Ben makes an irregular shape.
How do their areas compare?

options.why: Assumes a regular rectangular outline covers more despite both arrangements using identical pieces.
Assumes a longer irregular boundary creates more area without adding any pieces.

options.text: The shape with larger perimeter has larger area
options.why: Confuses perimeter with area; rearrangement can change boundary length while preserving total surface.

questions.solution_text:
Both use the same pieces exactly once, so their total covered surface is unchanged.
Their areas are equal.
